A Structural Term's Parameters, With Standard Errors

Source: R/structural.R
statmod_structural_table.Rd

Returns the estimated parameters of every structural term, on their own scale, together with standard errors and intervals that are taken from the joint observed information.

Usage

statmod_structural_table(fit, level = 0.95)

Arguments

fit

A StatmodFit().

level

The interval's level, 0.95 by default.

Value

A data frame with one row per quantity that each structural term reports and the columns parameter, term, name, estimate, se, lower, upper, held (the quantity is a held parameter), edge (it depends on a coordinate past the edge of its chart), component and position (the one of the term's own parameters to which the quantity belongs, and where in the parameter vector it sits; both are read off the Jacobian's support). The value is NULL where the model carries no structural term.

Details

A structural term contributes no design block, so the coefficient tables do not report it. statmod_full_information() spans the coefficients and the term's own parameters, and the tail block of its inverse (with the penalty Hessians added) is the variance of those parameters on the unconstrained scale. A covariance class split between the coefficients and the term's own parameters is placed by joint_penalty_at(), as in vcov.StatmodFit().

The quantities reported are those of modelterms7::term_readable(), which are not always the coordinates on which the term was estimated (a persistence of a score-driven term is an autoregressive coefficient, a function of the partial autocorrelations). The standard error of a quantity is the delta method over the joint variance of the term's parameters, \(\sqrt{J V J^\top}\), with \(J\) the Jacobian that term_readable() returns (a persistence of a term with \(q > 1\) reads several coordinates). The interval is built on the scale that the term declares for the quantity (for a score-driven term, the log scale for a positive loading, the scale of the partial autocorrelation's link for the persistence when \(q = 1\), and the identity scale for a persistence when \(q > 1\)): the standard error is carried to that scale by the derivative of its link and the end points are mapped back. The interval of a persistence is therefore confined to \((-1, 1)\) only when \(q = 1\).

A level held because an intercept in the same equation carries it is not estimated, and its standard error is reported as missing, as is that of any quantity whose Jacobian row reads a held parameter.

A quantity that depends on a coordinate past the edge of its chart (see structural_edge_rows()) is reported without a standard error and an interval, for the reason that a correlation at the boundary is: the chart's derivative tends to zero there, so the delta method reports a standard error that collapses exactly where the quantity stops being identified.

See also

statmod_full_information() for the joint matrix inverted, coef.StatmodFit() for the same parameters without their uncertainty
